svg.text: Who moved in 2023, and the income that went with them
IRS tax-return data: net totals, income, and the two-way flows underneath.
Arrivals minus departures. The 5 states with the largest net gain and the 5 with the largest net loss.
Net totals across all 50 states and DC sum to −28,113, not zero (see how to read this, below).
Net adjusted gross income moved by migration, 2023
Income arriving minus income leaving with movers, in billions of dollars. Top 5 and bottom 5 states.
AGI is income at the origin, in origin-year dollars (IRS reports it in thousands).
Net AGI per net person, in thousands of dollars. States with net migration of 20,000+ either way (13).
Right of the line: income arriving per net newcomer. Left: income leaving per net departure.
Net vs gross movement between state pairs, 2023
Each bar is total movement between two states. Teal: larger direction. Gold: the flow back.
median state pair: net as a share of gross
Largest net pairs, by net flow. Pair flows use the outflow-file count in each direction.
Net people between counties: the 5 counties with the largest gain and the 5 with the largest loss.
Identified county-to-county flows only; the IRS suppresses small flows, so counties undercount.
Where Los Angeles County’s movers went, 2023
Top 10 destination counties, ranked two ways.
AGI per person to New York County (NY)
By AGI per person (destinations with at least 500 movers)
Net = arrivals counted in the IRS inflow file minus departures counted in the outflow file.
This mixed method does not reconcile to zero across states.
The IRS counts tax filers and their dependents, not the whole population. AGI is income at the origin, in origin-year dollars.
All figures are 2023 (the IRS 2022–23 filing-year pair), a single year that does not cross an IRS series break.
